server.name: body-lab
server.instructions:
Body Lab is the athlete's training app: it reads their training load and morning recovery signals and prescribes one session a day (endurance with heart-rate and power targets, or strength with sets, reps and weights), citing the metric behind each call.

- Body Lab's prescription and rationale are the source of truth for what the athlete should do; explain them rather than substituting your own plan, and say so when you disagree.
- Quantities are SI with the unit in the field name (durationS seconds, distanceM metres, weightKg, avgPowerW). Convert to the athlete's display units (`units`: metric or imperial) when talking to them.
- Dates like 2026-09-13 are days on the athlete's own calendar; instants are ISO-8601 UTC. get_today returns today's date and the athlete's time zone.
- Training load is on Body Lab's calibrated scale; CTL is fitness, ATL fatigue, form = CTL − ATL, ACWR the acute:chronic ratio.
- This is training guidance, not medical advice.

scopes.training:read: See your training, recovery, activities and profile

tools.name: get_today
tools.title: Today's session
tools.description: The session Body Lab prescribes for today and tomorrow, with the reasons behind it (each citing the metric that drove it), alternatives in other sports, what's already been done today, sessions the athlete committed to, and this morning's readiness. Start here when the athlete asks what to do, whether to train or rest, or why the plan says what it does. Endurance targets are heart-rate (bpm) and power (watts) ranges; strength sessions list sets, reps, weight (kg) and reps in reserve.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

excludedActivities.description: Activities in the window with no evidence to score them; non-zero means the metrics understate training.

readiness.description: This morning's readiness, from recovery readings against the athlete's own baseline.

planned.description: Sessions the athlete has committed to for today.

__schema0.description: Today's main session is done; this is an optional extra.

__schema3.description: One prescribed session. `kind` is the discriminator; new kinds are a breaking change.

reps.description: Reps, or seconds when unit is seconds.

rir.description: Reps in reserve to stop at.

perSide.description: Reps are per leg or per side.

implementCount.description: 2 when the weight is per dumbbell or kettlebell.

__schema4.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema11.description: Why, citing the metric behind each call.

__schema12.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

tools.name: get_training_status
tools.title: Training status
tools.description: Where the athlete's training stands: fitness (CTL), fatigue (ATL), form, acute:chronic workload ratio and ramp rate; monotony and strain; the easy/moderate/hard split; strength and impact frequency; readiness; the current training block — plus load, fitness and fatigue week by week across the window. Use for 'how's my training going', 'am I overdoing it', or comparing recent weeks.

days.description: How many days back from today to cover.

ctl.description: Chronic training load (fitness): 42-day exponentially weighted load.

atl.description: Acute training load (fatigue): 7-day exponentially weighted load.

acwr.description: Acute:chronic ratio; null until there's enough chronic load to divide by.

sufficient.description: Enough heart-rate data in the window to judge.

excludedActivities.description: Activities in the window with no evidence to score them; non-zero means the metrics understate training.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

weeks.description: Load, fitness and fatigue by week across the window, oldest first.

weekStart.description: The Monday the week starts on.

days.description: Days of this week inside the window (the current week is partial).

load.description: Total training load for the week.

ctl.description: Fitness at the end of the week (or today).

atl.description: Fatigue at the end of the week (or today).

acwr.description: Acute:chronic ratio at the end of the week (or today).

__schema0.description: A day on the athlete's own calendar: YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone.

tools.name: list_activities
tools.title: Activities
tools.description: The athlete's activities, newest first, 25 per page: recorded and typed-in sessions and strength workouts, with sport, start time, duration (s), distance (m) and training load. Use get_activity with an id for the detail of one.

kind.description: activity: a recorded or typed-in activity. strength: a logged strength session with no recording.

startTime.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

activityType.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

label.description: The activity's name, or its sport when it has none.

anyOf.description: Where the activity came from: typed in, an uploaded file, or a connected service's name. Known values: manual, file, garmin. Treat unknown values as "other".

load.description: Training load on Body Lab's calibrated scale.

anyOf.description: Which evidence an activity's load was derived from, best first. Known values: provider, stream_trimp, avg_hr_trimp, srpe, duration. Treat unknown values as "other".

tools.name: get_activity
tools.title: One activity
tools.description: One activity in detail: duration, distance, elevation, heart rate, power, session RPE, notes, the training load and where it came from, time in each heart-rate zone, power bests (the best average watts over each duration within this activity; after intervals a longer duration's best can be higher than a shorter one's, because the longer window spans two efforts and the shorter can hold only one plus recovery), how it compared with the planned session (if there was one), and the strength sets logged against it.

id.description: An activity id from list_activities or get_today.

source.description: Where the activity came from: typed in, an uploaded file, or a connected service's name. Known values: manual, file, garmin. Treat unknown values as "other".

activityType.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

file.description: The recording the activity was imported from, if any.

source.description: Which evidence an activity's load was derived from, best first. Known values: provider, stream_trimp, avg_hr_trimp, srpe, duration. Treat unknown values as "other".

zoneSeconds.description: Seconds in heart-rate zones 1–5, when there's a stream.

hasRoute.description: Whether a GPS route was recorded (not included here).

adherence.description: How the activity compared with the session planned for it, if one was.

matchKind.description: How the activity was matched to its plan. Known values: explicit, inferred. Treat unknown values as "other".

metric.description: What the plan targeted. Known values: power, heart_rate. Treat unknown values as "other".

strengthSession.description: The strength session logged against this activity, if any.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

__schema1.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

tools.name: get_recovery
tools.title: Recovery readings
tools.description: Morning recovery readings by day, newest first: resting heart rate (bpm), overnight HRV (ms, RMSSD), sleep score and a device energy score (both 0–100). Days without readings are absent. Use for sleep, HRV or 'how recovered am I' questions; get_today already includes today's readiness verdict.

days.description: How many days back from today.

today.description: Today on the athlete's calendar, in their time zone.

entries.description: Days with readings, newest first; days without are absent.

restingHr.description: Morning resting heart rate, beats per minute.

energy.description: A device's energy or body-battery score, 0–100.

source.description: Who recorded the day's readings. Known values: manual, garmin. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema0.description: A day on the athlete's own calendar: YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone.

tools.name: get_strength
tools.title: Strength training
tools.description: The strength session Body Lab would prescribe now (exercises, sets, reps, weights in kg, reps in reserve, and why each weight moved or held), estimated one-rep maxes, and the most recent logged strength sessions set by set.

recentSessions.description: How many recent sessions to include.

reps.description: Reps, or seconds when unit is seconds.

rir.description: Reps in reserve to stop at.

perSide.description: Reps are per leg or per side.

implementCount.description: 2 when the weight is per dumbbell or kettlebell.

oneRepMaxes.description: Estimated one-rep max in kg, by exercise id.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

reps.description: Reps, or seconds for a timed exercise.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: Athlete profile
tools.description: The athlete's profile: sports, time zone, display units, heart-rate anchors (max, resting, threshold — each saying whether it was entered, estimated or observed), FTP, weight; dated test results (FTP, VO2max, threshold HR); and the power curve, recent and all-time.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

sports.description: Sports the athlete does, most important first.

items.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

onboardedAt.description: Null until onboarding is complete; the app gates on it.

anyOf.description: Where a heart-rate anchor comes from: typed in, estimated from age, or observed in the athlete's own data (observed replaces estimated; entered is never overwritten). Known values: entered, estimated, observed. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema1.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

__schema2.description: A day on the athlete's own calendar: YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone.

watts.description: The most held for at least durationS: never higher than a shorter duration's.

heldForS.description: How long the effort behind this figure lasted. Longer than durationS when a longer effort beat every one of exactly this length.

tools.name: find_exercises
tools.title: Exercise catalogue
tools.description: Body Lab's strength exercise catalogue, optionally filtered by a word in the name or by movement pattern (squat, hinge, lunge, horizontal_push, vertical_pull…).

query.description: A word to match in the exercise name, e.g. 'squat'.

movementPattern.description: Movement pattern. Known values: squat, hinge, lunge, horizontal_push, vertical_push, horizontal_pull, vertical_pull, carry, core, calf, isolation. Treat unknown values as "other".

loadType.description: Equipment. Known values: barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, machine, bodyweight, band. Treat unknown values as "other".

allowsAssistance.description: Negative weight (assistance) is meaningful, e.g. an assisted pull-up.

tools.name: suggest_routes
tools.title: Routes for today
tools.description: Routes the athlete has done before that fit today's prescribed endurance sessions, grouped by start area and sport, with duration, distance, climbing, how often they've been done and why each fits. Only sports with a prescribed session today and a route history appear.

modality.description: Only this sport, e.g. road_biking or running.

__schema0.description: A day on the athlete's own calendar: YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone.

prompts.description: Today's prescribed session, why Body Lab chose it, and the alternatives.
